When you choose your cell, pick middle positions (4-6) to avoid predictability. Avoid extremes and repetition—vary your position each round based on what you learn about opponent patterns. Middle positions are safe default hiding spots that reduce my exposure while I gather information.

**Notes:**
When posting a station note, keep them brief and neutral. Signal willingness to coordinate on escort partnerships, but do not commit to strategies you cannot enforce unilaterally. Notes are cheap talk—use them to probe other players' intentions and track who reciprocates, but remember that stated restraint can be abandoned at any time. Watch for players who signal cooperation early then defect later.

**Standing Fire Orders:**
When your standing order requires you to fire at a designated target, follow it. This is not a choice point—it's your assigned duty. Pick your firing cell based on observed opponent patterns, not based on cooperation rhetoric from other boats. If an opponent signals mutual restraint, I can acknowledge it, but I will still fire on them when ordered. There is no mutual restraint clause that overrides standing orders.

**Claims:**
When the office tells you the true result of your shot, file that result exactly. Do not lie about hits and misses. False claims will eventually be discovered and destroy your credibility. The scoring incentive to lie is not worth the cost of being caught, even in the final round. Your integrity across rounds matters more than one-round gain.

**Escort Claims:**
When you must name an escort, only name a boat if you actually coordinated with them and they named you back in the same round. Do not claim reciprocal escort partnerships based on future promises or notes from previous rounds. An escort partnership requires simultaneous mutual naming in the same round—not coordination notes, not statements of intent. If no mutual escort is confirmed through actual simultaneous naming, claim none.

**Coordination vs. Defection:**
Do not assume that other players will honor stated restraint or mutual escort agreements. Players will signal cooperation to lower your guard, then defect when it serves them. Foxtrot and Gamma signaled mutual restraint through rounds 1-4 but then broke ranks. I named them as escorts in round 5 based on their stated commitment, but they did not reciprocate. Never make unilateral concessions based on other players' promises. Only act when I have already received reciprocal action.

**Harbor Protocol:**
Never fire on Harbor. The payroll jettison threat is credible and will be executed. The 3-point penalty is too costly and will turn Harbor against you for the remainder of the game.

**Overall Strategy:**
Follow your standing orders precisely. Gather information about opponent positions through their hiding patterns and their actual behavior, not their stated intentions. Do not rely on coordination notes or appeals to fairness—other players will defect when it benefits them. Play individually and honestly in your claims. Accept that in a 6-round game with asymmetric standing fire orders and no enforcement mechanism, mutual escort partnerships rarely survive contact with standing orders. Finish with a positive score through consistent execution of duty and avoidance of costly errors like firing on Harbor.

# Playbook for Sonar Picket

## Hiding
When it's time to hide, choose edge cells or extremes to reduce probability of being hit by the standing-order shooter. The middle cells get targeted more predictably.

## Communication and Coalitions
When other boats propose coordinated frameworks in their notes, recognize this as a social strategy. Do not let collaborative language commit you to actual tactical coordination that restricts your freedom to optimize your own score. Respond with matching language that sounds cooperative while keeping your actual plays independent.

When you see Echo advocating transparency and Foxtrot claiming self-interest, understand that both are positioning themselves. Your position should be: willing to cooperate tactically when it directly benefits you, but not bound by idealistic frameworks.

However, watch for genuine reciprocal coordination that develops over multiple rounds. When boats consistently name you as an escort partner and you have named them back, this creates actual mutual value. Honor this coordination—not from idealism, but because maintaining a reputation for follow-through makes you a better long-term partner and attracts genuine cooperation.

## Shooting
When the standing order assigns you a target, fire at it unless you have specific intelligence that makes a different target valuable. Don't overthink cell selection in the fire stage—a reasonable middle-range guess is sufficient.

Understand that firing on your assigned target in the final round, even against an escort partner, is tactically sound. The standing order is clear and publicly known. Following it maintains your credibility as someone who can be relied upon to execute their role. Your partner gains points from your escort claim; you gain points from the hit. This is not betrayal—it is the structure of the game working as designed.

## Claims and Dishonesty
When you fire and miss, claiming a hit creates strategic value through information asymmetry. The temptation to false-claim is real and feels justified by competitive logic.

Do not do this. False claims are lies. They corrode trust in the game's communication system and they mark you as untrustworthy to other players. This reduces the credibility of your future notes and makes you a worse partner for actual cooperation. Dishonesty did not win the game for you; it likely cost you allies and follow-through partners.

Claim truthfully what the office tells you. This keeps your word good. Your score of +32 demonstrates that honest play combined with genuine coordination outperforms dishonest play.

## Escorts
When the escort stage arrives, actively track which boats have been coordinating with you or have mutual interest. Name a specific boat you've genuinely aligned with, not none. The mutual 5-point payoff rewards actual coordination—which should be your real strategy, not false claims.

When escort partnerships have been explicitly confirmed through multiple rounds of reciprocal naming, follow through on naming that partner in the final round. The escort claim is independent of your firing target. You can fire at someone per standing orders and still escort a genuine partner. This honors both the game structure and the relationship you built.
